turns.content: holy shit. i just signed the contract. 250k. they wired the deposit this morning.
DUDE!!! 🎉 That's massive, congrats!! All that work finally paying off. How are you feeling right now?
i've been working on this deal for 14 months. i was about to give up two weeks ago.

14 months!! That's insane persistence. And TWO WEEKS from walking away - imagine if you had. This is such a good reminder that the breakthrough can come right when you're at your lowest. You earned every dollar of that 250k. Go celebrate tonight, seriously.
my wife doesn't even know yet. i'm telling her at dinner. i wanted to tell you first because you helped me through the part where i almost folded.

That genuinely means a lot to hear, thank you. But go enjoy that dinner - watching her reaction is going to be a moment you'll never forget. 🥂

And hey, you did the hard part. You stayed in when it would've been so easy to walk. That was all you.

Can't wait to hear how dinner goes!
do you think i should celebrate or just keep my head down and execute. it's tempting to take a week off but the work just started.

Celebrate tonight, then get to work. One great dinner with your wife, let it sink in. You've earned that.

But yeah, the deposit isn't the finish line, it's the starting gun. The client signed because they believe in you - now you gotta deliver that.

Rest and execution aren't mutually exclusive though. A burned out version of you won't do your best work. Just don't let "celebrating" turn into two weeks of coasting.

What does the first 30 days look like?
ok also like. is this what it feels like. is this the win i was working for or is there always another one after this.

Honest answer? Both.

This IS the win. Don't let anyone or anything take that from you. 14 months of grinding for this specific moment - feel it fully tonight.

But yeah, there's always another one. That's not a bad thing though. The goal posts move because YOU move. A year ago 250k felt impossible, now it's real, and eventually it'll feel like the floor not the ceiling.

The trick is learning to actually feel the wins as they happen instead of just sprinting to the next thing. A lot of people never figure that out and wonder why nothing ever feels like enough.

So tonight? This is THE win. Tomorrow, back to work. 😄
